entities.name: Luca Ridolfucci Gentili
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Cardinal Luca Ridolfucci Gentili (b. c. 1350, Camerino – d. January 26, 1389, Rome) was a prominent Italian cardinal and bishop whose brief but impactful career unfolded during the tumultuous Western Schism. This period profoundly reshaped the political and religious landscape of late medieval Europe, and Ridolfucci Gentili's ecclesiastical ascent from Bishop of Camerino to Cardinal-Priest of San Sisto exemplified the complex interplay between papal authority, local power structures, and the personal ambitions of prelates in the 14th century.

Elevated to the episcopate as Bishop of Camerino in 1378 by Pope Urban VI, Ridolfucci Gentili quickly became a key supporter of the Roman pontiff in the escalating conflict against the Avignon papacy. His unwavering loyalty was rewarded with the cardinalate on December 17, 1381, a promotion that solidified Urban VI's faction within the College of Cardinals. He participated in various curial activities, serving as a papal legate and advisor, particularly concerning the ecclesiastical administration of central Italy and efforts to solidify Urban VI's position against Clement VII, the Avignon claimant.

Ridolfucci Gentili's cardinalate contributed to the institutional hardening of the Western Schism, as his elevation reinforced the legitimacy claims of the Roman line of popes. His career, marked by staunch allegiance to Urban VI, showcased the personal stakes involved in the schism, where ecclesiastical advancement often depended on political alignment. The administrative structures he helped maintain, even in a divided Church, indirectly laid groundwork for future reconciliation efforts by preserving the Roman curial tradition and its network of loyalists.
